entities.summary:
Lorenzo Campeggio (1485-1539) was an Italian cardinal and politician.




He was appointed as the cardinal protector of England by Pope Clement VII in 1532, a position he held until his death in 1539. This appointment made him the last cardinal protector of England and marked a significant shift in the relationship between the Catholic Church and the English monarchy.




Campeggio played a key role in the politics of the Holy Roman Empire during the 16th century, serving as a diplomat and advisor to various European monarchs. His legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he helped shape the course of European politics and the role of the Catholic Church in England.




As a cardinal, Campeggio was deeply committed to the preservation of Catholic doctrine and practices, and he worked tirelessly to promote the interests of the Catholic Church throughout Europe.




Despite his significant contributions to the history of the Catholic Church, Campeggio's own life and legacy have been somewhat overshadowed by that of other historical figures. Nevertheless, his impact on European politics and the role of the Catholic Church in England remains an important chapter in the story of the Church's influence on Western civilization.
